Looking at the demo: the grid splits into a left block, a separator column (2), and a right block. Output has the width of each block; cells where the left and right cells are equal become 3, otherwise the shared color (4 in demo, 0 in test).

```python
def transform(grid):
    H = len(grid)
    W = len(grid[0])
    # find separator column: column with a single distinct color spanning full height
    sep = None
    for j in range(W):
        col = set(grid[i][j] for i in range(H))
        if len(col) == 1 and all(grid[i][j] != grid[i][0] or True for i in range(H)):
            # candidate; check it differs from neighbors typically
            sep = j
    # more robust: separator is column where all cells equal each other
    for j in range(W):
        if all(grid[i][j] == grid[0][j] for i in range(H)):
            sep = j
            break
    lw = sep
    rw = W - sep - 1
    left = [row[:lw] for row in grid]
    right = [row[sep+1:sep+1+rw] for row in grid]
    left_colors = set(c for row in left for c in row)
    right_colors = set(c for row in right for c in row)
    shared = left_colors & right_colors
    base = min(shared) if shared else 0
    out = []
    for i in range(H):
        row = []
        for j in range(lw):
            if j < rw and left[i][j] == right[i][j]:
                row.append(3)
            else:
                row.append(base)
        out.append(row)
    return out
```
